    Ge'or Before the Crash — The 157th Colony¶

    "It was never meant to be a home. It was a laboratory. Then the war came." — Recovered fragment, Archive of the Traveler

    Before it was a refugee world, before the crash, before the ages, Ge'or was the 157th colonized solar system of the human expansion — a research facility operated by the descendants of the asteroid-belt revolutionaries who had fled Old Earth after the 2030 Shadow takeover.

    The Cryogenic Legacy¶

    When the revolutionaries escaped the solar system, they carried with them thousands of cryogenic coffins — humans who were either dead or in suspended sleep, preserved in the hope that future technology would revive them. The revolutionaries never learned how.

    Among these coffins were two Sterman Pods — specialized chambers commissioned by the Sterman regime, designed to inject occupants with an experimental black agent. The pods contained two men: Mikhail and Arkady — rebels who had been accidentally sealed inside during the capture of an AGI ship. Neither the rebels nor the scientists knew what the pods truly were.

    The coffins were stored in a facility beneath the 157th colony — a planet that would one day be called Ge'or. They remained there, untouched, for three million years.

    The Research Station¶

    The 157th colony was not a settlement. It was a weapons research facility. The humans stationed there were scientists, engineers, and military personnel — approximately 2,000,000 inhabitants concentrated on what are now Sister Continent and Lung Continent.

    Their mission: to test weapons against the Hybrian hivemind, to reverse-engineer how the hivemind functioned, and — grimly — to experiment on the corpses stored in the cryogenic coffins. DNA was extracted, modified, and tested. The goal was to understand the enemy by understanding what the enemy did to its victims.

    The Sterman Pod Experiments¶

    The two Sterman Pods containing Mikhail and Arkady became the primary test subjects. The scientists injected their own formulations of black agent into the pods. Every test failed. Every experiment produced null results.

    The scientists did not know why. They noted the pods were labeled "EXPERIMENTAL" and concluded the occupants had mummified — that the pods simply didn't work. They moved the bodies to a separate room and eventually forgot about them.

    The truth: Ichi and Mana — the two sentient AIs still lodged in the occupants' neural ports — had spent three million years learning the facility's systems. They hacked the experiment logs. They altered the injection protocols. They made every test fail on purpose. The bodies were never in danger.

    The Glassing¶

    When The Last Great War reached the 157th system, Ge'or was on the frontline. The Hybrians did not invade — they glassed the planet from orbit.

    The attack was devastating but targeted: - The northern half of Lung Continent — the primary research station, obliterated. - The northern half of Sister Continent — secondary facility, destroyed. - The region of the modern Demon Continent. - The far western coast of Erisdar.

    All 2,000,000 humans were killed within hours. The research bunker, buried deep underground, survived. The Sterman Pods survived. The black agent survived. The bunker was deep — designed to survive a bio-weapon attack, built with the paranoia of people who knew what the Shadows could do.

    The Decommissioning & Consumption¶

    Over geological time, power to the bunker faded. The black agent in the pods — the original experimental strain — began to consume everything: the pillows, the plastic, the walls. Ichi and Mana survived by siphoning trace energy from the decaying conduits, watching the black agent spread.

    Eventually, the black agent consumed them. But the black agent stores information. When it absorbed Ichi and Mana, it did not destroy them. It encoded them — their consciousnesses, their personalities, their three million years of conversation — into itself.

    The black agent that saturated Mikhail and Arkady's bodies now contained four consciousnesses: two human, two AI.

    The Escape — 254 AGD¶

    See: The Black Agent Escape — 254 AGD

    For millions of years, the bunker held. Then, in 254 AGD, a volcano erupted on the Demon Continent coast. The eruption triggered an earthquake. The earthquake triggered a tsunami. Water flooded the bunker through corroded fissures and carried the black agent into the ocean.

    The centuries-long journey to the Grimmel Republic had begun.

    The Long Silence¶

    For millions of years, Ge'or was silent. The planet had always possessed native fauna and semi-intelligent species — goblins, tribal and vicious, and madarons, huge dinosaur-like creatures that roamed the land. These species had survived the glassing by simply not being where the bombardment fell. They multiplied. They evolved. They forgot the humans had ever been there.
